title: Many Americans 'Work Remotely' from the Office
paragraphs: Every morning, you wake up early, get ready in a hurry and make the long commute to the office — only to spend the next eight hours talking to colleagues through a screen.
According to a new report called Remote Work from the Office, this routine has become normal for many Americans.
Researchers from the Federal Reserve Bank of New York and the University of Virginia surveyed over 1,800 US workers in September this year.
On their most recent day in the office, nearly half had no in-person meetings. Seventy-one percent were missing at least one teammate, while 15% had no casual face-to-face conversations with anyone.
And here's the interesting part: 37% joined at least one online meeting even though everyone taking part was in the same office.
"These workers commute in just to work remotely from the office," the researchers said.
One reason is that team members often work in different offices or cities, so even when employees show up, their colleagues may be far away.
Another is poor planning. Some companies require a certain number of office days but let workers choose when to come in. As a result, teammates often miss each other.
And some employees simply prefer video calls even when everyone is in the same office, because sharing screens can make it easier to work together.
Companies often say office time helps people share ideas, learn from one another and build relationships. But just getting people through the office door may not be enough.
